title: A New Detection Method Defining the Aerobic Threshold for Endurance Exercise and Training Prescription Based on Fractal Correlation Properties of Heart Rate Variability
authors: Rogers B, Giles D, Draper N, Hoos O, Gronwald T
population: 15 participants performing an incremental treadmill run with gas exchange and HRV recording (single-session method comparison)
findings: The VO2 and HR at which DFA a1 first reached 0.75 (HRVT) were compared with those at gas-exchange VT1.
Mean VT1 was reached at 39.8 ml/kg/min and HR 152 bpm versus HRVT at 40.1 ml/kg/min and HR 154 bpm, with no difference by t test.
Pearson r was 0.99 for VO2 and 0.97 for HR; intraclass correlation 0.99 for VO2 and 0.96 for HR.
The authors conclude DFA a1 reaching 0.75 on an incremental treadmill test is closely associated with crossing VT1.
limitations: Small sample (n = 15), single incremental treadmill test; no repeat tests or fatigued state; the abstract does not report the Bland-Altman limits of agreement (see Van Hooren 2023 for those).
implications: Where beat-to-beat RR data from a chest strap exist, DFA a1 = 0.75 can be offered as an optional data-driven estimate of the HR at VT1 (Zone 1 upper boundary), shown alongside other estimates, not as the sole definition.
Do not compute DFA a1 from optical wrist HR; require RR-interval data with artifact correction. No other DFA a1 cut-off is justified by this paper.

verification.notes: Crossref: Front Physiol vol 11, issued 2021-01-15 (article number carries 2020). Abstract confirms numbers. Design relabelled from experimental-crossover to other (single-session method comparison). The wrist-HR statement is an engineering inference, not in the abstract.
